name: slack
summary: Slack's hosted MCP server (search, read and post messages) with your own Slack app
notes: You create the Slack app first (no dynamic client registration): an internal app in your workspace or a directory-published app; Slack forbids unlisted apps from using MCP. Your workspace admin may need to approve it.

In the Slack app, turn on PKCE (OAuth & Permissions, or pkce_enabled: true under oauth_config in the manifest) and add the redirect URL http://localhost:8977/callback. Slack treats a localhost redirect as a desktop redirect only once PKCE is on; without it Slack demands https. Turning PKCE on makes the app a public client and cannot be undone without Slack support; refresh tokens then expire after 30 days and the app cannot ask for bot scopes on this redirect.
lotr setup slack asks for the app's client id and secret as references (Slack's MCP authorization server lists only client_secret_post).

Scopes are user-token scopes: this template asks to search public channels, read public channels and their history, look up users and post messages. Add the search:read.private / groups:* / im:* / mpim:* scopes only if you mean to reach private channels and DMs.

Posting a message (send or schedule) is an ordinary write here; it does not ask first. Anything that deletes, removes, archives or kicks asks first (consent). Slack's documented tool set has no delete tool.
offline_access is off: Slack does not use that scope. Long-lived sign-in depends on whether token rotation is enabled on your Slack app.
Slack's docs name tools by description, not by tool name, so no smoke op is set.
